title: Mumbai Metro
description: Rapid transit system in Mumbai, India
wiki_lead:
The Mumbai Metro is a rapid transit train system serving the city of Mumbai and the wider Mumbai Metropolitan Region in Maharashtra, India. The system consists of 4 colour-coded lines serving 77 stations with a length of 91.48 km (56.84 mi) as of April 2026. It is India's third largest and third busiest metro system. The metro has a mix of underground, at-grade, and elevated stations using standard-gauge tracks.
The rapid transit metro system is designed to reduce traffic congestion in the city and supplement the overcrowded Mumbai Suburban Railway network. When completed, the core system will comprise sixteen high-capacity metro railway lines, spanning a total of more than 523 kilometres (325.0 mi) (25% underground, the rest elevated, with a minuscule portion built at-grade) and serviced by 350 stations.
Construction work began in February 2008, and the Blue Line, the system's first, commenced operations on 8 June 2014. Many lines were subsequently delayed because of late environmental clearances, land acquisition troubles, and protests. Sections of 2A and 7 were inaugurated on 2 April 2022. A section of the Aqua Line was inaugurated on 5 October 2024 and a year later the line became fully operational. On 7 April 2026, sections of 9 and 2B were inaugurated. Additionally, there are 8 other metro lines currently under construction in the city.
Three separate agencies are responsible for Mumbai Metro's operations: Line 1 is operated by Mumbai Metro One Private Limited (MMOPL), a joint venture between Reliance Infrastructure (74%), the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (26%) and formerly by RATP Dev Transdev Asia (5%). The completely underground lines 3 and 11 will be built by Mumbai Metro Railway Corporation Ltd (MMRC). The rest of the system, consisting of lines 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and their extensions are being built by the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) and operated by the Maha Mumbai Metro Operations Corporation Limited (MMMOCL). While the Maharashtra Metro Rail Corporation Limited (Maha Metro) is responsible for all metro rail projects being developed in the rest of Maharashtra, the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority is the authority responsible for maintaining the metro system in the Greater Mumbai area.

History
Being the capital of Maharashtra, Mumbai is among the largest cities in the world, with a total metropolitan area population of over 2 crore (20 million) as of 2011, and a population growth rate of around 2% per annum. Mumbai has the advantage of a high modal share of the public (88%) in favour of a public mass transport system.  The existing Mumbai Suburban Railway carries over 70 lakh (7 million) passengers per day, and is supplemented by the Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST) bus system, which provides feeder services to station-going passengers to allow them to complete their journeys. grok_lead: The Mumbai Metro is a rapid transit rail system designed to serve the densely populated Mumbai metropolitan region in India, addressing severe road congestion through a network of elevated and underground lines. Operational since 2014, it currently spans multiple corridors with a combined track length exceeding 60 kilometers, facilitating efficient mass transit for commuters in one of Asia's busiest urban centers. The system's inaugural line, Line 1 (Blue Line), an 11.4-kilometer elevated route connecting Versova to Ghatkopar via Andheri, commenced commercial service on 8 June 2014 after a trial run in May 2013, marking Mumbai's entry into modern metro rail operations under a public-private partnership model. Subsequent phases have added lines such as 2A (Dahisar East to D.N. Nagar) and the fully operational Aqua Line (Line 3) in October 2025, a 33.5-kilometer underground corridor from Colaba to SEEPZ that represents India's longest subterranean metro stretch. Envisioned in a 2005 master plan by the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation as nine corridors totaling 146.5 kilometersâwith 32.5 kilometers undergroundâthe project has delivered notable infrastructure achievements, including daily ridership peaks surpassing 400,000 passengers and integration with Mumbai's existing rail networks to cut travel times and vehicular emissions. Nevertheless, development has been marred by protracted delays, land acquisition disputes, and substantial cost overruns; for instance, Line 3's expenses escalated by approximately â¹14,000 crore amid construction halts linked to political shifts and activist interventions. These issues highlight systemic challenges in executing large-scale urban infrastructure in India, including bureaucratic inefficiencies and environmental litigation, yet the metro's expansions continue to advance connectivity for Mumbai's over 20 million residents.
